newsitem.title: TURKEY: SOCCER-UEFA CONFIRMS EXPANSION OF CHAMPIONS' LEAGUE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-UEFA CONFIRMS EXPANSION OF CHAMPIONS' LEAGUE.

text.p: The European Champions' League will increase from 16 to 24 teams from the 1997-98 season, UEFA's executive commitee confirmed on Thursday.

European soccer's governing body, meeting in this Mediterranean resort, said the competition would be played in six groups of four teams, with the six group winners and the two best runners-up progressing to a knock-out stage.
At present teams play in four groups of four with two sides from each group qualifying for the quarter-finals.

UEFA, who dumped champions from smaller nations out of the European Cup two years ago, said the decision to change the format meant all domestic champions would have a chance to qualify for the Champions' League.
In addition Europe's top-eight ranked countries will be able to enter a second team for the qualifying phase.

The current top nations who stand to benefit by having a second team in the competition are Italy, Spain, the Netherlands, England, France, Germany, Portugal and Belgium, although this list could vary slightly by the start of the 1997-98 season.
A UEFA working group first proposed the idea of a 24-team competition in May.
The expanded format means a flurry of matches over the European summer with a preliminary round involving champions from 32 countries to be played in July.

The 16 winners then play a qualifying round in August with eight of the remaining national champions plus eight additional high-placed teams. The winning 16 teams would then join the eight remaining champions for the group stages.
The Champions' League began with just eight clubs in the 1992-93 season.
